Hi Jinhui,

 

The current CODEX assumes at least one latent factor (K>=1). For your purpose, you can source the attached normalize0.R and use the command below:

 

> normObj <- normalize0(Y_qc, gc_qc, K = 0)

 

The subsequent code should be the same as what you can get from the vignette.

 

Cheers,

Yuchao

From: Zhang, Nancy [mailto:n...@wharton.upenn.edu]

Cc: Yuchao Jiang
Subject: RE: about method CODEX

 

Dear Jinhui,

 

Thanks for your interest in CODEX.  Unfortunately, I think 6 exomes is too small for CODEX to reliably estimate most of the bias parameters.  As we show in our paper, CODEX combines data across samples to estimate the latent effects.  We need at least 20-30 samples for the latent effects to be estimated well.

 

However, I have an idea for your data.  We can try to set “K”, the number of latent variables, to 0 for your data.  Then, CODEX only estimates the GC function and exon specific factors, which is feasible with 6 exomes.  This sub-component in the model usually captures a large portion of the bias in the data.  Certainly, the results won’t be as good as if you do the full-scale normalization, but it may be sufficient for what you want to accomplish. 

 

Yuchao:  Do you think this is possible within the CODEX package?

 

Nancy

Subject: about method CODEX

 

Dear Dr. Zhang,

 

I am writing to you to inquiry whether the CODEX method developed by your lab can be applied to small sample sets.

 

We have 6 whole exome sequencing data, 3 affected samples and 3 unaffected samples from 2 families.

 

Family 1: A1 is affected and her mom U1 is not affected

Family 2: A2 is affected. Her dad U2 and her mom U3 are not affected. She also has a distant relative A3 who is affected.

 

We are looking for CNVs shared between the affected individuals and not in present in non-affected ones.

 

Could you let us know whether CODEX method is feasible for our project?  If not, could you please kindly help to point to the methods useful? Any your suggestions are highly appreciated.

 

Sincerely,

Jinhui Ding, Ph.D.

Laboratory of Neurogenetics, NIA, NIH
